name: Lemp Mansion
unique: A brewery family's mansion where several members died by suicide, now a restaurant and inn with ghost tours, dinner theater and overnight rooms that guests leave early.
buzz: The dinner mystery is campy and the history is genuinely tragic; overnight guests report doors and footsteps. Book the tour before you commit to a room.

name: The Stanley Hotel
customer: Stephen King fans, couples, ghost hunters
unique: The grand hotel that inspired The Shining, with a nightly ghost tour through the concert hall, the tunnels and room 217, plus a hedge maze and mountain views.
buzz: The tour is more history than scare and that is why it works; the hotel itself is worth a drink even if you do not stay.

name: Crescent Hotel
unique: A limestone hotel built as a cancer cure, later a college and a scam, now a haunted hotel with a ghost tour that climbs to the fifth floor and the morgue in the basement.
buzz: The tour guides are performers and the building has real stories; the town of Eureka Springs is worth the weekend on its own.

name: Whaley House
unique: A brick Greek Revival house built on a former gallows site, called the most haunted house in America, with tours through the courtroom, parlor and family bedrooms.
buzz: It is small and the ghost stories are well documented; evening tours are spookier. Old Town around it is a good half day.

name: Queen Mary
unique: A 1936 ocean liner turned hotel, with engine rooms, a first class dining room and haunted ship tours that go into the bow and the pool, where guests report voices.
buzz: The ship is magnificent and the ghost tour is theatrical but rooted in real accidents; the hotel rooms are uneven.

name: Sallie House
unique: A small Victorian house where a young girl is said to have died during an appendectomy, now rented by the night for investigations with a binder of reported activity and no caretaker on site.
buzz: It is not a show, it is a house, and that is what makes it unsettling. Serious investigators book weeknights and bring their own equipment.

name: Pennhurst Asylum
unique: A haunted attraction inside a real abandoned institution for people with disabilities, with tunnels, wards and a history that is darker than any actor in makeup.
buzz: The setting does most of the work and the history is worth reading before you go; some visitors find the spectacle uncomfortable given the real suffering.

name: Centralia
unique: A town mostly erased by an underground coal fire that has burned since 1962, with a few streets, a cemetery and graffiti on the closed highway, watched over by a handful of residents.
buzz: It is eerie and quiet and you should stay on the road; the fire is still burning and the ground is unstable. A sobering detour, not a playground.

name: St. Augustine Lighthouse
company: St. Augustine Lighthouse and Maritime Museum
unique: A black and white striped lighthouse with a maritime museum and a dark of the moon ghost tour, where staff report footsteps on the tower stairs and a girl in the basement.
buzz: The climb is worth it for the view alone; the ghost tour is one of the better researched ones in Florida. Book after dark.

name: House of Yes
unique: A warehouse in Bushwick putting on circus, burlesque, immersive theater and themed parties with aerialists over the crowd and a strict no phones policy.
buzz: The productions are wildly creative and the crowd dresses for it; shows sell out and the space gets packed. Check the dress code before you go.

name: The Slipper Room
unique: A tiny burlesque and variety club on the Lower East Side with a velvet stage, a live band and acts that range from classic tease to sword swallowing.
buzz: The room is intimate and the performers are professionals; get a table early and tip well. A reliable weird night out.

name: Superblue Miami
unique: A warehouse of immersive light and sound installations, including a mirrored infinity room and a cloud sculpture you walk through, designed by artists rather than set builders.
buzz: The mirrored room is the photo everyone wants and the timed entry keeps it calm; it is short for the price. Pair with the Design District.

name: ARTECHOUSE
unique: A subterranean digital art space under the Mall where projectors turn the walls and floor into a moving environment, with a different artist each season.
buzz: The scale is impressive in a small room; shows change often so check what is running. Good rainy day option.

name: Mint 400
unique: A desert off road race for trucks, buggies and motorcycles across hundreds of miles of Mojave, with a pit area you can walk and a contingency parade down Fremont Street.
buzz: The trucks are enormous and the jumps are violent; spectating requires a map and a four wheel drive. The Fremont Street parade is free.

name: King of the Hammers
unique: A week long off road festival in the desert where rock crawlers and trophy trucks race over trails that combine boulders and open desert at speeds that should not be possible.
buzz: It is a temporary city in the sand and the racing is savage; bring an RV, water and ear protection. Spectating is free and the nights are a party.

name: Pikes Peak International Hill Climb
unique: A 12.4 mile race to the 14,115 foot summit with 156 turns, no guardrails in places and a history that includes dirt, pavement and fatal crashes.
buzz: The altitude and the drop offs make it unlike any other race; get a spectator pass and take the shuttle. Weather can cancel the day.

name: Bonneville Speed Week
unique: A week on the salt flats where home built streamliners, roadsters and motorcycles run flat out for records, and anyone with a car and a license can take a rookie pass.
buzz: The cars are extraordinary and the pits are open; the salt destroys everything it touches. Bring sunscreen, shade and a hat.

name: Rooster Cogburn Ostrich Ranch
unique: An ostrich ranch beside the interstate where you hand feed ostriches, donkeys and parakeets from a cup, with a monster truck tour and a petting area.
buzz: It is silly and cheap and kids talk about it for years; the birds are aggressive in a funny way. A good break on the drive to Tucson.

name: Virginia Safari Park
unique: A 180 acre drive through safari where bison, zebra and elk stick their heads in your car, plus a walk through village with giraffes and kangaroos.
buzz: Buy the feed and accept that your car will be licked; the drive through is the fun and the walk through is a bonus. Go early.

name: Safari West
unique: A 400 acre wildlife preserve in the wine country with giraffes, rhinos and antelope, visited by safari truck, plus tent cabins if you want to wake up to the sounds.
buzz: The safari is genuinely good and the glamping is the splurge; the animals have space and the guides know them by name.

name: Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center
unique: A drive through refuge for injured and orphaned Alaska animals, with bears, moose, musk ox and wood bison in large enclosures against the mountains.
buzz: The setting is spectacular and the animals are visible from the road; it is a refuge, not a zoo, and the staff explain why. Worth the drive from Anchorage.

name: Bearizona
unique: A drive through wildlife park with black bears, wolves and bison roaming large forest enclosures, plus a walk through section with otters and jaguars.
buzz: The drive through is the draw and the bears come close to the car; the walk through is smaller. A good stop on the way to the Grand Canyon.

name: Lakota Wolf Preserve
unique: A wolf preserve where you sit on benches inside the enclosure while timber, arctic and tundra wolves circle and howl, guided by keepers who raised them.
buzz: The howl is the moment everyone remembers and the photography is extraordinary; book the morning tour and follow the rules.

name: Sky Falconry
unique: A hawk walk where a trained Harris hawk flies to your gloved fist and follows you across a hillside, with lessons on how raptors hunt and why falconry works.
buzz: Feeling the bird land on your arm is the whole thing; the guides are patient and the views are a bonus. Book the early slot.

name: Bengies Drive-In
unique: The largest drive in screen in the country at 120 feet, with a strict no talking, no headlights rule and a snack bar that still makes real food.
buzz: The rules are enforced and that is why the picture is good; arrive early for a good spot and tune the radio. A time machine.

name: The Big Texan Steak Ranch
unique: A highway steakhouse with a 72 ounce steak challenge, a shooting gallery, a gift shop and a limo with longhorn horns, all visible from I-40 for a hundred miles.
buzz: The challenge is a spectacle and the regular steaks are fine; watch someone attempt it, tip the servers and skip the souvenir hat.

name: Field of Screams
customer: Haunted house fans, teens, young adults
unique: Four attractions on a farm, including a haunted hayride through the woods, a den of darkness and a corn maze, run with a level of set design that has kept it nationally ranked.
buzz: The hayride is the signature and the actors are relentless; go with a group and buy the combo pass. Lines peak after dark.
